pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Check, Please!
work.note: Check, Please! é uma websérie de quadrinhos sobre um jovem que aprende a se virar em restaurantes e encontros. A referência é uma expressão de restaurante, “Check, please!”, para dividir a conta.

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: At an American sandwich counter, you make many small choices: bread, cheese, vegetables and a side. Learn the questions and answers so you can order lunch quickly.

facts.big: At a sandwich shop, you can choose your bread.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: The server asks: white, wheat or another bread.

facts.big: Many restaurants give you a box for your leftovers.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: You can ask, “Can I get a box, please?”

facts.big: You can say “Check, please!” to ask for the bill.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: In the USA, the bill at a restaurant is called the check.

facts.label: Educação e tom
facts.sub: Answer each question with a short choice and please: Wheat, please. At the end, say Thanks!

compare.br: In Brazil, lunch is often a hot meal of rice, beans and meat, sometimes a self-service “por quilo” restaurant.
compare.us: In the USA, lunch is often a sandwich, a salad or a quick meal, and it is shorter. You build it with questions and choices.
compare.tip: Do not say “yes” to every question; choose: “Wheat, please.”
compare.ask: What is your favorite lunch? Say it in English.

pages.title: Lunch in Los Angeles · 1/3
paragraphs: Today I am in **Los Angeles**, and it is lunchtime. My friends say, “**Let’s grab lunch!** I know **a great spot**.” We walk to a small sandwich shop near the beach.

The line is short. A man behind the counter says, “Hi! What can I get you?” I say, “**Can I have** a turkey sandwich?” “**White or wheat?**” “Wheat, please.” “**Any cheese? Lettuce? Tomato?**” “Yes, all of them.” “**Fries or a salad?**” “A salad, please.” Then he says, “**Enjoy your lunch!**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Lunch in Los Angeles · 2/3
paragraphs: My friend Mia orders chicken, and Ben orders a cheese sandwich. It is not expensive, and it is **super tasty**. We sit outside and eat in the sun.

The comic “Check, Please!” by Ngozi Ukazu started in 2013. In it, a college student called Eric loves to bake, joins a hockey team and makes new friends. The title is a joke: a “check” is a hockey move, and “Check, please!” is also what you say at a restaurant.

pages.title: Lunch in Los Angeles · 3/3
paragraphs: After lunch, I say, “**Check, please!**” and the waiter brings the bill. We **split the check**. It is easy: everybody pays for their own food. I leave a small tip, and we walk to the beach.

items.why: Split the bill = each person pays a part.
